questions.knowledgeNote: Break the function rule on purpose: give one input two outputs (or leave an input with none).
questions.question: AQ1(b)(i). Give a relation from A to B which is NOT a function.
questions.solution: E.g. R = {(a,x),(a,y),(b,z)}: the input 'a' has two images (x and y), so R is not a function. (Any relation where some element of A maps to two elements of B, or an element of A maps to nothing, works.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q1; book pp112-113 = PDF pp137-140

questions.knowledgeNote: A constant map (everything to one output) is the simplest function; a matching pairs all three.
questions.question: AQ1(b)(ii). Give relations from A to B which ARE functions.
questions.solution: E.g. R1 = {(a,x),(b,x),(c,x)} (constant function - every input maps to x) and R2 = {(a,x),(b,y),(c,z)} (one-one matching). In each, every element of A has exactly one image in B, so both are functions.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q1; book pp112-113 = PDF pp137-140

questions.knowledgeNote: Integers only: [1,6) contributes {1,2,3,4,5}. Evaluate piece by piece.
questions.question: AQ2. A function f is defined on the set of integers by f(x) = 1+x (1<=x<2), 2x-1 (2<=x<4), 3x-10 (4<=x<6). (a) Find the domain of f. (b) Find the range of f. (c) Is f one-one?
questions.solution: (a) Integer x with 1<=x<6: domain = {1,2,3,4,5}. (b) f(1) = 2; f(2) = 3, f(3) = 5; f(4) = 2, f(5) = 5. Range = {2,3,5}. (c) No: f(1) = f(4) = 2 with 1 != 4. Matches the printed Answers key (p115): 'Domain = {1,2,3,4,5), Range = {2,3,5); No'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q2; book pp112-113 = PDF pp137-140; every value matches printed Answers key p115 (PDF p142)

questions.knowledgeNote: Equal gaps (1,3,5,7...) mean linear: slope = step = 2.
questions.question: AQ3. Is f = {(1,1),(2,3),(3,5),(4,7)} a function? If it is defined by f(x) = ax + b, find a and b.
questions.solution: Yes: each x (1,2,3,4) occurs once, so f is a function. a(1)+b = 1 and a(2)+b = 3 give a = 2, b = -1. Check: f(3) = 5 and f(4) = 7. So a = 2, b = -1. Matches the printed Answers key (p115): 'a = 2, b = -1'.

questions.knowledgeNote: Read each arrow diagram three ways: every input hit exactly once (function?), outputs covering B (onto?), distinct outputs (one-one?).
questions.question: AQ4. Three print arrow diagrams are given. State whether each is (i) one-one and onto, (ii) an into function, (iii) an onto-only function; show by diagram and give the domain and range of each.
questions.solution: Method (diagrams are print figures - pending physical-book read): (i) one-one and onto = every element of A maps to a distinct element of B and every element of B is hit (bijective, sets match in size); (ii) into = some element of B is never hit (range is a proper subset of B); (iii) onto-only = every element of B is hit but two inputs share an output (many-one). Domain = the full left set; range = the hit elements of B in each diagram. FLAGGED: exact sets pending figure read.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q4; book p113 = PDF pp138-140; statements are print figures

questions.knowledgeNote: Squares forget signs: (-1)^2 = 1^2 kills one-one immediately.
questions.question: AQ5 (T.U. 2049). Let A = {-1,-2,0,1,2} and f:A->B be defined by f(x) = x^2/2. Find the range of f. Is the function one-one?
questions.solution: f(-1) = 1/2, f(-2) = 2, f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1/2, f(2) = 2. Range = {0, 1/2, 2}. Not one-one: f(-1) = f(1) = 1/2 with -1 != 1. Matches the printed Answers key (p115): 'Range = {0,1/2,2}, No'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q5 (T.U. 2049); book p113 = PDF pp138-140; matches printed Answers key p115 (PDF p142)

questions.knowledgeNote: Six inputs, six distinct outputs: one-one holds, but B has a seventh member (1) nobody hits - so 'both' fails.
questions.question: AQ6 (T.U. 2050, 2058S). Let f:A->B be defined by f(x) = (x-1)/(x+2) with A = {-1,0,1,2,3,4} and B = {-2,1,-1/2,0,1/2,1/4,2/5}. Find the range of f. Is f one-one and onto both? If not, how can it be made so?
questions.solution: f(-1) = -2, f(0) = -1/2, f(1) = 0, f(2) = 1/4, f(3) = 2/5, f(4) = 1/2. Range = {-2,-1/2,0,1/4,2/5,1/2}. All six outputs are distinct, so f is one-one; but 1 in B is never hit, so f is not onto (hence not both). Fix: replace B by the range (drop 1); then f:A->range is one-one and onto. Matches the printed Answers key (p115).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q6 (T.U. 2050, 2058S); book p113 = PDF pp138-140; matches printed Answers key p115 (PDF p142)

questions.knowledgeNote: The print renders f(x) = x/(x+2) (OCR reads it as '(2+x)/x'; the printed Answers key forces x/(x+2) - every value matches).
questions.question: AQ7 (T.U. 2051). Let f:A->B be defined by f(x) = x/(x+2) with A = {-1,0,1,2,3,4} and B = {-1,0,1,1/3,1/2,3/5,2/3}. Find the range of f. Is f one-one and onto both? If not, how can it be made so?
questions.solution: f(-1) = -1, f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1/3, f(2) = 1/2, f(3) = 3/5, f(4) = 2/3. Range = {-1,0,1/3,1/2,3/5,2/3}. All six distinct: one-one yes; 1 in B is never hit: onto no (so not both). Fix: replace B by the range (drop 1); then f is one-one and onto. Matches the printed Answers key (p115). (Print-form note: the scan renders the rule ambiguously; x/(x+2) is adopted because it reproduces the key exactly.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q7 (T.U. 2051); book p113 = PDF pp138-140; rule adopted via printed Answers key p115 (PDF p142)

questions.knowledgeNote: Linear with nonzero slope is always bijective on Q: solve y = 3x+5 for x to exhibit the pre-image of every y.
questions.question: AQ8. Let Q be the set of all rational numbers. Show that f:Q->Q with f(x) = 3x + 5 is one-one and onto. (The book prints a full model solution.)
questions.solution: One-one: let x1, x2 in Q with f(x1) = f(x2): 3x1+5 = 3x2+5 gives 3x1 = 3x2, so x1 = x2. Onto: for each y in Q, x = (y-5)/3 is in Q and f(x) = y. Hence f is one-one and onto. (Reproduces the book's printed solution, book p113.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.2 Additional Q8; book p113 = PDF pp138-140 (solution printed in book)
